prerequisites: Mastery of Continuum Mechanics / Elasticity and Strength of Materials I
Mechanics (statics, shear, bending, and axial force diagrams)
Full knowledge of force calculation and hypostaticity/hyperstaticity
Having passed Elasticity and Strength of Materials II is strongly recommended

learning_outcomes.text: Classify and select the most suitable structural typologies for industrial building and installations.
Identify, evaluate and combine the design actions and loads acting on a construction, applying the applicable technical regulations (CTE, Eurocodes, etc.).
Model and calculate stresses and deformations in industrial structures using manual structural calculation methods.
Collaborate proactively in the development of work, setting goals and meeting objectives.
Contribute to the search for solutions to challenges or projects, demonstrating empathy and assertiveness when sharing ideas, reflections and arguments within collaborative work.
Structure the discourse to facilitate the understanding of the objectives, actions and/or results of one's own work.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.
Dimension and check metallic and reinforced concrete structural elements according to Ultimate Limit State (ULS) and Serviceability Limit State (SLS) conditions.
Design and interpret the plans for structures and foundations of an industrial building.

teaching_methods: Group work (preparation of essays, problem solving, projects)
Individual study (preparation of readings, exams, exercises, class preparation)
assessment_rules: For the first call, the final grade is the sum of teamwork (25%), the final exam (50%), and the integrated project (25%). The exam is split into two partials. A total grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass. If the integrated project (PI) is not completed, a minimum of 4 in each partial and practical assignment submission is required to average with the rest. For the second call, students can choose to keep the grades from the integrated project and teamwork (each 25%), in which case a 50% weighted exam will be taken, and previously approved partials can be kept. If these grades are not kept, the exam will weigh 100% of the final grade.
